options.option_text: Wise (synonym — both mean showing careful good judgement)
Reckless (correct: prudent = showing care and thought for the future; reckless = without thinking of consequences ✓)
Cautious (synonym — both mean careful/wary)
Judicious (synonym — both mean showing good judgement)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PRUDENT = acting with care and thought for future consequences. Antonym = RECKLESS = not giving thought to consequences; impulsive. Other antonyms: imprudent, foolhardy, careless. Synonyms of prudent: wise, judicious, cautious, sensible.

options.option_text: Strict (synonym — austere can mean strict/severe)
Luxurious (correct: austere = simple and plain, without comforts; luxurious = comfortable and expensive ✓)
Stern (synonym — stern = strict/serious)
Ascetic (synonym — ascetic = practising self-denial, like austere)

questions.explanation: B is correct. AUSTERE = lacking comforts or luxuries; simple, strict, or severe. Antonym = LUXURIOUS = full of comfort, indulgence, and wealth. Other antonyms: lavish, extravagant, comfortable. Synonyms: austere, ascetic, spartan, stern.

options.option_text: Obedient (synonym — docile = ready to obey/submissive)
Intractable (correct: docile = easily managed/obedient; intractable = hard to manage/control ✓)
Compliant (synonym — compliant = willing to comply)
Submissive (synonym — both mean easily controlled)

questions.explanation: B is correct. DOCILE = ready to accept control/instruction. Antonym = INTRACTABLE = difficult to manage or control; stubborn. Other antonyms: unruly, obstinate, recalcitrant, defiant. Synonyms of docile: obedient, submissive, compliant, manageable.

options.option_text: Frank (synonym — frank = open and honest, like candid)
Evasive (correct: candid = truthful and straightforward; evasive = avoiding direct answers ✓)
Sincere (synonym — sincere = genuine and honest)
Blunt (synonym in spirit — blunt means direct/frank)

questions.explanation: B is correct. CANDID = truthful and straightforward; frankly honest. Antonym = EVASIVE = not direct or straightforward; avoiding honest answers. Other antonyms: dishonest, deceptive, indirect. Synonyms: frank, forthright, open, blunt.

options.option_text: Thriftiness (synonym — both mean economical use of resources)
Extravagance (correct: frugality = careful and economical use of resources; extravagance = excessive spending ✓)
Economy (synonym — economy of means = frugality)
Austerity (synonym — austerity = frugality imposed by necessity)

questions.explanation: B is correct. FRUGALITY (noun) = the quality of being economical with money. Antonym = EXTRAVAGANCE = excessive expenditure; wastefulness. Other antonyms: lavishness, profligacy, prodigality. Synonyms of frugality: thriftiness, economy, parsimony.

options.option_text: Impoverished (synonym — both mean extremely poor)
Opulent (correct: penurious = extremely poor; opulent = ostentatiously rich ✓)
Destitute (synonym — both mean without resources)
Indigent (synonym — indigent = poor and needy)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PENURIOUS = extremely poor; also can mean miserly. Antonym = OPULENT = ostentatiously rich; luxuriously wealthy. Other antonyms: affluent, prosperous, wealthy. Synonyms of penurious: destitute, impoverished, indigent, poverty-stricken.

options.option_text: Wasteful (synonym — prodigal = wastefully extravagant)
Frugal (correct: prodigal = spending money or resources freely and recklessly; frugal = economical ✓)
Lavish (synonym — lavish = sumptuously generous)
Spendthrift (synonym — spendthrift = person who spends money recklessly)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PRODIGAL = wastefully extravagant. Famous: 'The Prodigal Son' who squandered his inheritance. Antonym = FRUGAL = carefully economical. Other antonyms: thrifty, parsimonious, miserly. Note: 'prodigal' doesn't mean 'one who left and returned' (a common confusion).

options.option_text: Sullen (synonym — sullen = bad-tempered and gloomy)
Gloomy (synonym — both mean dark/sullen in mood)
Jovial (correct: morose = sullen and gloomy; jovial = cheerful and friendly ✓)
Melancholic (synonym — melancholic = deeply sad/gloomy)

questions.explanation: C is correct. MOROSE = sullen and ill-tempered; gloomy. Antonym = JOVIAL = cheerful, friendly, and in a good mood. Other antonyms: cheerful, buoyant, exuberant, elated. Synonyms of morose: sullen, gloomy, melancholic, moody, surly.

options.option_text: Indifferent (synonym — callous = showing no feeling; indifferent = having no interest)
Empathetic (correct: callous = insensitive and cruel; empathetic = understanding and sharing feelings ✓)
Apathetic (synonym — apathetic = lack of interest or feeling)
Insensitive (synonym — both mean not feeling others' pain)

questions.explanation: B is correct. CALLOUS = showing or having no sympathy for others; cruel. Antonym = EMPATHETIC = showing empathy; understanding and sharing others' feelings. Other antonyms: compassionate, sensitive, caring, humane. Synonym-trap: all wrong options are synonyms of callous.

options.option_text: Voluble (synonym — voluble = talking fluently and at length)
Talkative (synonym — both mean very chatty)
Laconic (correct: garrulous = excessively talkative; laconic = using very few words ✓)
Loquacious (synonym — loquacious = very talkative)

questions.explanation: C is correct. GARRULOUS = excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters. Antonym = LACONIC = using very few words; brief and to the point. Other antonyms: reticent, taciturn, terse, reserved. Synonym-trap: voluble, talkative, loquacious are all synonyms of garrulous.
